title: Al Capone Was Brought Down by Income Tax
description:
Al Capone ran the Chicago Outfit from 1925 to 1931. After seven rival gangsters were murdered in 1929 and newspapers named him Public Enemy No. 1, the Treasury and Justice Departments planned income tax prosecutions. He was charged with 22 counts of tax evasion, his own admissions of his income were admitted as evidence, and in 1931 he was convicted of five counts and sentenced to 11 years. He served in Atlanta, then Alcatraz, was released after almost eight years and died in 1947. Facts from Wikipedia's article on Al Capone; pictures from Wikimedia Commons (all public domain), credited on screen and below.
